Hi Aaron / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a set of technical questions that will help us finalize a Dedicated capacity proposal tailored to FinOptics' production profile.

What we covered (brief):
- Demo: embeddings + reranking pipeline, chat with structured tool-calls for downstream enrichment.
- Key goals you stated: sub-200ms median for sync rerank calls, <250ms for live chat responses in primary region, index 75M vectors with near-real-time upserts, and predictable monthly spend.

Open technical details we need to confirm (please reply inline where helpful):
1) SDK + Auth
   - Languages: do you want official SDKs (Python/Node) or only REST?
   - Auth: will you require customer-managed mTLS (mutual TLS) for Private/Dedicated, or standard API keys with VPC peering + KMS?

2) Routing & Regions
   - Primary region: you mentioned us-west-2; confirm fallback to eu-west-1 acceptable for failover.
   - Are you okay with an automated region-failover policy (active-primary, passive-fallback) or do you want manual control?

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - Preferred output format: function-calling JSON schema vs free-form JSON? We recommend schema-first for deterministic parsing in your enrichment pipeline.

4) Embeddings & rerank throughput
   - Target QPS: you mentioned 50 concurrent rerank requests and 300 embedding requests/sec peak — confirm peak vs sustained.
   - Do you plan to batch embedding uploads client-side (recommended) or stream single-item inserts?

5) Dedicated capacity sizing (initial proposal assumptions)
   - Concurrency per replica: assume 8 concurrent generation/rerank workers per GPU replica for sync paths.
   - Autoscale policy: scale +1 replica per 120 qps of sustained emb/serving load, cool-down 60s, max 12 GPUs (configurable).

Action items / next steps
- Aaron/Priya: answer the 5 quick confirms above by EOD Wed so we can lock the Dedicated sizing.
- Redwood: we will produce an updated proposal and an ops-runbook (attachment: integration-checklist.xlsx) within 48 hours.

Attachments: finoptics_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal draft), integration-checklist.xlsx
Recording: call recording referenced as recording-20270801.mp4 (we'll share link on Drive).

My proposed Dedicated sizing (initial) — input requested:
- Model choices: embeddings model E-1 (FP16 quantized) for vectorization; rerank/generation model R-1 (8-bit quantized) for sync paths.
- Replica sizing: 1 GPU replica = p4d-equivalent 1 unit (we'll map to our flavor during quoting).
- Concurrency: 8 sync slots per replica for rerank/generation; embedding throughput per replica (batched): ~1200 embeddings/sec at batch size 64 (estimate).
- Autoscale: target headroom = 25% above peak sustained (per Aaron: peak 300/sec), so initial commit = capacity for ~400 embeddings/sec sustained.
- Max replicas: 12 (covers bursting to 2-3x for short periods with queueing).
- Queue strategy: token-aware front-door queue with per-customer rate limits, queue depth 1000 requests, per-request TTL 8s for sync rerank then failover to async retry path.

Questions for infra:
- Karthik: can we support mTLS with automated cert rotation tied to the customer's KMS? If not, what's the manual rotation runway?
- Sean: confirm embedding batch latency trade-offs at batch size 64 vs 32 for their latency targets. Any changes to concurrency assumption?

Please add comments — I want to include the final numbers in the updated proposal for Aaron.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: FinOptics — post-demo recap & technical asks (needs sizing + mTLS)

Marissa — quick notes from infra/serving POV after a 20m sync with ops:

- mTLS: we can support mTLS for Dedicated deployments via customer-provided certs; cert-rotation options:
  * Manual rotation: customer uploads new certs via console/API (supported today).
  * Automated rotation: we can integrate with external CA (ACME) in Q4 roadmap, but not in GA for Private yet.
  * Workaround: Redwood can host short-lived intermediate cert and rotate using KMS APIs; requires 30-day lead and an SOW addendum.

- Concurrency & batching: embedding batch size 64 yields ~batch latency 50-70ms and higher throughput; at 120/second sustained per GPU replica is conservative. For p50 rerank 180-200ms we need low batching on the sync path (batch size <=8) and reserving dedicated slots. So keep concurrency=8 for sync rerank and reserve 2 slots per replica for unbatched low-latency calls.

- Autoscale math (proposal):
  * Use customer-defined target (sustained) 120/s embeddings -> estimate 1 replica per 120 sustained embeddings (batched). For their peak 300/s, initial commit = 4 replicas (480 capacity) to keep headroom.
  * Max replicas = 12 as requested; cool-down = 60s. Fallback policy: overflow to hosted pool with soft-failover (best-effort latency degraded).

- Queueing: implement per-route queue with 1000 depth, prioritization token for sync rerank (TTL 8s). If queue TTL expires, switch to async webhook callback path.

I'll draft short text for the proposal describing the mTLS constraints and rotation options. Sean, please sanity-check the numbers for GPU flavor mapping and embedding throughput.

Karthik
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference

Aaron / Priya — attaching an updated proposal (finoptics_proposal_v2.pdf) and the integration checklist. Summary of the changes based on your asks and infra input: 

1) Auth & cert rotation
   - We support mTLS for Dedicated. Options: manual cert rotation via console/API (supported now) or a managed rotation path (requires SOW addendum). We'll include both options in the proposal.

2) Dedicated sizing (recommended initial commit)
   - Initial commit: 4 GPU replicas (p4d-equivalent) mapped to our in-quote SKU.
   - Rationale: supports ~480 embeddings/sec batched (headroom for 300/s peak, sustained ~120/s) and 32 dedicated sync rerank slots (8 slots/replica) to meet p50 180-200ms.
   - Max replicas: 12 (burst/auto-scale). Autoscale: +1 replica per 120 sustained embeddings, cool-down 60s.

3) Queue & fallback
   - Per-customer front-door queue depth 1000, sync TTL 8s -> on TTL expiry fall back to async webhook or hosted fallback models (best-effort).

4) Routing & region
   - Primary region: us-west-2 with passive fallback eu-west-1. Auto-failover mode is opt-in; default will be active-primary with manual failover.

5) SDK & structured output
   - We'll deliver Python + Node SDKs in the onboarding bundle. For structured output we recommend JSON schema (function-calling) and provide examples in the proposal.

Next steps:
- If you confirm mTLS + the initial commit numbers, we'll issue an updated contract and DocuSign draft (link included).
- Proposed time to finalize contract: 1 week after confirmation; we can support an accelerated procurement path if needed.
